name: Factory and manufacturing
purpose: machine safety, lockout tagout, quality and defects, near-miss reporting, PPE, process alarms, lean and continuous improvement

scenes.what: the lidding machine on filling line 2 seen from its operator side at mid distance: its guard enclosure with a closed interlocked door, the electrical cabinet built into its right end with the main isolator, and the conveyor running on to the check-weigher
scenes.for: lockout and tagout, safe jam clearing, machine guarding and interlocks, emergency stops, isolation before maintenance
plan: Seen from above, metres: x runs along the line to the right; y runs from the camera toward the hall's north side wall at y 9.5 (blockwork to 2.4 m, cladding above; the frame's columns at x 0.0 and 7.5 just inside it; the light blue air main at 3.2 m). The line's front is at y 6.0, its back at 7.8.

The lidder's guard enclosure from x 0.0 to 2.6, 2.2 m high: solid light grey panels to 1.0 m, clear polycarbonate above in aluminium frames; a pair of guard doors across its front, hinged at their outer edges (x 0.3 and 2.3) and meeting in the middle at x 1.3, the right-hand door with a grab handle near its free edge (x 1.45, 1.3 m) and an interlock switch at the top of the meeting line (x 1.35, 2.05 m); the touch screen on a swing arm at its left end (x 0.4, 1.5 m up); a red emergency stop on yellow on its right front corner at 1.2 m; its andon tower at x 2.4, 2.8 m up. Inside: the lid magazine and the pressing head over the conveyor.

The lidder's electrical cabinet is built into the enclosure's right end, x 2.6 to 3.6, from 0.3 to 2.0 m, its door facing the walkway: the main isolator (a red rotary handle on a yellow plate) at x 3.35, 1.3 m; two small indicator lamps at its top right (x 3.5, 1.9 m); the door handle at x 2.7, 1.1 m; a yellow electrical warning sign low on the door at about 0.7 m.

Right of the cabinet the conveyor runs on (top 0.9 m, rails to 1.1 m) from x 3.6 to beyond the right edge, carrying lidded tins; the check-weigher on it from x 4.6 to 5.8 with its control box on a post at its right end (top 1.4 m). Left of the enclosure, a short conveyor from the filler, whose enclosure's right end stands at x -0.6.
The floor in front is the operator zone (y 5.0 to 6.0); the walkway's yellow lines run just below the frame.

The walkway runs past the station from y 0 to 1.2; the station's zone, edged by a yellow line at y 1.2, runs from x -2.2 to 5.2 and back to the wall.

The bench: a stainless steel bench 1.8 by 0.75 m, top at 0.9 m, standing free from x 0.0 to 1.8 and y 2.2 (its front, toward the camera) to 2.95, with an undershelf: on it a precision scale (x 0.45, its display facing the camera), a tablet on a stand (x 1.45), a few sample tins with their lids off and a lid lever, and a jointed task lamp clamped at its right back corner (head at x 1.7, 1.4 m up).
Against the wall at the left, from x -1.9 to -0.7: a steel shelving rack 2.0 m high and 0.45 m deep holding rows of retained sample tins.

identity.place: A water-based paint plant on an industrial estate at the edge of a mid-sized town in a temperate country, about 25 years old, making emulsions and trim paints in 2.5 L metal tins for about 140 people over two shifts. Steel portal-frame halls under one roof: the filling hall (about 60 m long, 30 m wide and 8 m to the eaves) with two filling lines running along it; the process hall beside it, where tall stainless mixing vessels stand on a steel platform; and, between the two, a single-storey block of painted blockwork holding the control room, the welfare rooms and the corridor and PPE lobby that lead onto the filling hall.
architecture: hall walls in two bands: fair-faced concrete blockwork painted light grey from the floor to 2.4 m, then pale grey-white profiled steel cladding with vertical ribs up to the eaves at 8 m
the portal frame's grey steel I-section columns stand just inside the walls every 7.5 m, each with a yellow-and-black striped foot guard; no column stands inside a line or a walkway

the roof seen from below: grey liner on purlins, the frame's rafters, strips of translucent roof light, rows of round LED high-bay lights hung at about 7 m; along the walls at about 3.2 m a compressed-air main painted light blue and a galvanised cable tray above it

the floor: concrete with a mid-grey epoxy coating, smooth and slightly glossy; yellow lines 100 mm wide edge the 1.2 m walkways, which carry a white walking-person pictogram every 10 m; hatched yellow areas mark where nothing may stand

the filling lines: a chain of machines on conveyors at 0.9 m: a filler and a lidder inside guard enclosures (brushed stainless and light grey sheet panels to about 1.0 m, clear polycarbonate panels in aluminium frames above to 2.2 to 2.3 m, hinged guard doors with interlock switches), an open check-weigher on the conveyor with a reject bin, a labeller, and a palletiser inside a fence of black welded-mesh panels on yellow posts 2.0 m high; a three-lamp andon tower on each machine; red emergency stops on yellow at every station
the block between the halls: painted blockwork, doors in slate blue steel frames with narrow vision panels, a long internal window from the control room onto the process hall
identity.materials: Light grey sheet steel machine panels and electrical cabinets, brushed stainless steel at the product contact parts, clear polycarbonate guards in grey aluminium frames, black welded mesh fencing, mid-grey epoxy floor, light grey blockwork and pale cladding; slate blue as the company's colour (door frames, the team board's edging, the control-room console's end panels); silver metal paint tins with plain coloured bands and wire handles, white tin lids, tan cartons and pale pine pallets. Families: machine panels and cabinets in wall (their shade tones), stainless and aluminium in metal hi, mesh fencing in metal, polycarbonate in glass at low opacity, slate blue in wall2, tins in metal hi with plain bands of any palette tone, pallets in wood hi, cartons in wood. Safety colours only where they are in life: safety yellow (floor lines, posts, foot guards, warning signs, the yellow backing of emergency stops and isolators, hazard stripes) in the brass family; black on hazard stripes in metal deep; blue mandatory signs and the compressed-air main in the fabric family; green safe-condition signs and green lamps in plant hi; red emergency-stop heads, isolator handles, fire equipment, prohibition rings, lockout padlocks and red lamps in accent; white sign grounds and pictograms in paper.
inhabited: work in progress: a pallet of empty tins in layers with card sheets between them at the infeed, a stack of lids in a tray, a reel of labels on a spindle, a full pallet of cartoned tins waiting to be wrapped
the paperwork of the place, all as empty slots: a batch sheet in a clear pocket on each machine, the team board's charts and cards, the near-miss cards, a calibration sticker on the check-weigher

safety kit where it really is: red emergency stops on every station, a lockable isolator on every machine's cabinet, extinguishers on brackets with their red signs, a green first-aid sign, an eye-wash station by the process hall door, a spill kit in a yellow bin
wear: a few drips of paint wiped up under the filler, scuffed foot guards, the yellow line worn grey where trolleys cross it, a dented tin set aside on a shelf
scale: a person is about 1.75 m tall; the eaves are at 8 m, about four and a half people; a door is 2.1 m high and about 0.9 m wide
conveyor tops at 0.9 m with guide rails to about 1.1 m; guard enclosures 2.2 to 2.3 m high; perimeter fencing 2.0 m high, its mesh starting about 0.15 m above the floor
a 2.5 L paint tin is about 0.19 m across and 0.2 m tall; a pallet of filled tins in cartons stands about 1.3 m above a 1.2 by 0.8 m pallet
walkways 1.2 m wide between their lines; the team area beside a line about 3.5 m deep
emergency stops at about 1.0 to 1.3 m; machine touch screens at about 1.4 to 1.6 m; isolator handles at about 1.2 to 1.6 m; extinguisher handles about 1.0 m; signs at about 1.6 to 2.2 m
the control-room console's desk at 0.72 m with screens rising to about 1.3 m; the overview display in the control room about 3.1 m wide (two 65-inch screens side by side), its bottom at 1.4 m
identity.default_light: Even, cool white light from the rows of LED high-bay lights at 7 m, softened by daylight from the roof-light strips: light from almost straight above, so shadows are short and lie close under things (a contact shadow under each machine and pallet, the underside of each conveyor darker, the inside of a guard enclosure a step dimmer than the hall). Small lamps glow where they are on: the andon towers, the touch screens, the panel indicators.
identity.motifs: Use at least three of these in every scene so the sets belong to one place (each scene names the ones its camera can see): light grey machine panels with clear polycarbonate guards in aluminium frames, a three-lamp andon tower, red emergency stops on yellow, black mesh fencing on yellow posts, yellow walkway lines on the grey epoxy floor, silver paint tins with plain coloured bands, the light blue compressed-air main along the wall, slate blue door frames and edging.
avoid: a generic grey factory with no character, or a dirty, unsafe one (the plant is well run; the lessons are about people's choices in it)

objects.guard enclosure: a machine guard enclosure: a rectangular frame of grey aluminium extrusion standing on the machine base; brushed stainless or light grey sheet panels from the base to about 1.0 m, clear polycarbonate panels above to 2.2 to 2.3 m, a flat top panel; hinged guard doors on the operator side with a grab handle and a small interlock switch at the top corner of each door; fixing screws at the panel corners
objects.filler: a tin filler inside its guard enclosure: a row of stainless filling nozzles above the conveyor, each with a pneumatic valve body, fed from a small stainless bowl tank on top of the frame; tins pass under the nozzles on the conveyor; a drip tray under the nozzles; a touch screen on a swing arm at the enclosure's end
objects.lidder: a lidding machine inside its guard enclosure: a vertical magazine stack of white lids feeding a placing head over the conveyor, then a pneumatic pressing head that seats each lid; a tray of spare lids on a shelf on the enclosure
objects.check-weigher: an open check-weigher in the conveyor: a short belt section about 1.2 m long on a weigh cell, a small grey control box on a post at its end with a little display and an emergency stop, a pusher arm that sweeps rejected tins sideways into a grey plastic reject bin on the floor in front
objects.labeller: a wrap-around labeller inside a lower guard enclosure (2.0 m): a label reel on a spindle, a peel plate beside the conveyor and a pair of rubber belts that roll each tin past it; the reel and plate seen through the polycarbonate
objects.conveyor: a tabletop chain conveyor about 0.2 m wide with its top at 0.9 m: a stainless side frame on adjustable legs with round feet, white plastic guide rails on brackets either side at about 1.1 m, a drip tray underneath; tins stand on it in a single row
objects.andon tower: a stack light: three translucent round lamp segments (green at the bottom, amber, red at the top) about 70 mm across on a short black base and a slim pole, fixed on top of a machine at 2.6 to 2.9 m; only the lamp that is on glows
objects.emergency stop: a red mushroom-headed push button about 40 mm across on a round yellow backing plate, in a small yellow box or on a panel, at about 1.0 to 1.3 m where an operator can hit it
objects.touch screen: a machine touch screen about 0.4 m wide in a grey housing on a jointed swing arm, its centre about 1.5 m up, tilted toward the operator; its face a lit screen (paper hi) with a slot, no characters
objects.team board: a free-standing double-sided team board on two steel legs with feet: a board 2.4 m wide and 1.2 m tall, its bottom at 0.9 m, with slate blue edging; a near-miss card rack (rows of small pockets with cards), a chart area and a whiteboard, a narrow ledge along the bottom for markers
objects.paint tin: a round 2.5 L metal paint tin about 0.19 m across and 0.2 m tall: rolled rims at top and bottom, a silver body with a plain coloured band where the label goes (no print), a pressed-in lid, a wire carrying handle in two small ears
objects.floor markings: painted on the floor: solid yellow lines 100 mm wide edging walkways and zones; yellow and black diagonal striped lines where a rule starts (PPE beyond this line); a white walking-person pictogram about 0.6 m tall in a walkway every 10 m; never letters
objects.high-bay light: a round LED high-bay light about 0.4 m across, a finned dark aluminium body with a white diffuser underneath, hung from the roof steel at about 7 m in regular rows; seen from below as a bright disc
objects.electrical cabinet: a light grey steel electrical cabinet built into the machine's end: a single hinged door with a raised edge and a quarter-turn handle, a rubber seal line round the door, a cable gland plate underneath; on the door the main isolator, two small round indicator lamps and a warning sign
objects.isolator: a rotary main isolator: a red pistol-grip handle about 0.1 m long on a square yellow plate about 0.15 m across, fixed on the cabinet door; the handle turns a quarter turn between on (vertical) and off (horizontal); in the off position a slot lines up so a padlock shackle can pass through and hold it; a red padlock and a card danger tag hang from it only when it is locked out
objects.safety sign: an ISO 7010 pictogram sign, shape and colour by type and never any words: warning, a yellow triangle with rounded corners, a black border band and a black pictogram; mandatory, a solid blue disc with a white pictogram; prohibition, a white disc with a red ring and a red diagonal bar over a black pictogram; safe condition, a green square with a white pictogram; fire equipment, a red square with a white pictogram. Rigid panels about 0.1 to 0.4 m, screwed flat to a wall, a door or a post
objects.control console: a straight control-room desk 0.8 m deep with a laminate top at 0.72 m on a steel frame, slate blue end panels, a cable channel along the back edge with monitor arms clamped to it, a closed knee panel under the desk, a keyboard and a mouse at each position
objects.monitor: a 24-inch monitor about 0.55 m wide and 0.34 m tall with a thin dark bezel on a jointed arm, its lower edge about 0.88 m up, its face a lit screen (paper hi) with a slot when on
objects.overview display: two 65-inch screens side by side on low wall brackets, each about 1.45 m wide and 0.82 m tall with a thin dark bezel, their bottoms at 1.4 m; their faces lit screens (paper hi) with one slot over both
objects.task chair: a control-room task chair: a five-spoke base on castors, a gas-lift column, a padded seat about 0.47 m high with a waterfall front, a high padded backrest with a headrest, two armrests on posts
objects.desk phone: a dark grey desk phone with a corded handset on its cradle and a small screen, beside a radio standing in a desk charger with a short antenna
objects.wall clock: a plain round wall clock about 0.35 m across with a light frame and a white face carrying twelve short ticks and two hands, no numbers
objects.document cupboard: a tall light grey steel cupboard about 1.0 m wide, 0.45 m deep and 2.0 m high with two doors, a slim vertical handle and a small key lock
objects.ceiling grid: a suspended ceiling of 0.6 m square white tiles in a thin white grid at 2.8 m, with flat square light panels set into the grid in a regular pattern
objects.quality bench: a free-standing stainless steel bench 1.8 by 0.75 m with its top at 0.9 m: a flat top with a turned-down front edge, four square legs with adjustable feet, a solid undershelf about 0.15 m above the floor
objects.precision scale: a bench scale: a square stainless weighing pan about 0.3 m across on a low grey body, with a small display on a short stalk at its front, and a round level bubble on its top corner
objects.tablet on a stand: a tablet about 0.25 m wide in a grey rugged case, held at an angle by a weighted desk stand; its face a lit screen (paper hi) with a slot
objects.task lamp: a jointed bench task lamp: a clamp on the bench's edge, two slim arms with a spring, a small round shade, its light pooled on the bench top
objects.sample rack: a steel boltless shelving rack about 1.2 m wide, 0.45 m deep and 2.0 m high, light grey uprights with perforations and five shelves, each shelf a neat row of retained 2.5 L tins with plain labels
objects.quarantine cage: a lockable mesh cage about 1.2 by 1.2 m and 1.8 m high: square steel tube posts and frames painted red, filled with welded wire mesh, a hinged mesh gate on its front with a drop bolt and a hasp for a padlock; it stands on the floor inside a painted red line
objects.pallet load: cartons of tins in a stable block on a 1.2 by 0.8 m pale pine pallet, about 1.3 m high, wrapped in clear stretch film that shows as soft diagonal highlights; a plain white label rectangle on the face
objects.ppe dispenser: a wall-mounted PPE cabinet about 1.1 m wide and 0.6 m tall, light grey steel with a clear acrylic front divided into compartments: rows of safety glasses and over-glasses in an open tray, a round rotary ear-plug dispenser with a turning handle, a box of disposable gloves in a holder; a small shelf underneath
objects.mandatory signs board: a white rigid board about 1.1 m wide and 0.7 m tall fixed to the wall, carrying a row of five blue mandatory signs (solid blue discs about 0.2 m across with white pictograms of a face with glasses, a head with ear defenders, a boot, a gloved hand and a work coat), no words
objects.personnel door: a single steel door 1.2 m wide and 2.1 m high in a slate blue steel frame: a narrow vertical vision panel of wired glass, a stainless push plate and pull handle, an overhead door closer arm, a kick plate at its foot
objects.coat hooks: a slate blue wooden rail with a row of steel double hooks at 1.75 m, hung with spare high-visibility visitor vests in safety yellow with silver reflective bands
objects.hand sanitiser: a white wall-mounted sanitiser dispenser about 0.12 by 0.25 m with a push bar and a small indicator light, fixed at about 1.2 m
objects.bench and mirror: a slatted timber bench on a steel frame, seat at 0.45 m, against the left wall; above it at the far end a full-length mirror about 0.6 m wide in a thin frame from 0.5 to 2.0 m
